title: trim-runtime-bloat-lightweight-instrumentation-adapter-and-metrics-pipeline-slimdown
creator: Diego Alvarez
description:
Problem: The platform's tracing and metrics stack has accumulated heavyweight dependencies (multiple OpenTelemetry SDKs, vendor wrappers, and opinionated exporters) that increase worker binary size, warmup latency, and CPU overhead on high-throughput inference paths. This ticket extracts a minimal thin-trace adapter and consolidates exporter wiring to reduce runtime overhead while preserving existing observability semantics and downstream compatibility.

Goals: 1) Introduce a small, dependency-light trace/metrics adapter (trace-shim) used by hot path services to emit spans and counters into an internal proxy. 2) Pin and upgrade core OpenTelemetry libraries in control-plane services to a vetted set (OTEL 1.13.x for Go + 1.7.x for Node) with known performance patches. 3) Replace in-process bulk exporters with a single async exporter process (metrics-stitch) that batches and forwards to our telemetry backend to reduce tail latency and memory churn. 4) Maintain all existing span attributes and sampling policies; validate with end-to-end regression tests and eval prompts.

Approach:
- Implement trace-shim (Go) with a tiny API surface: StartSpan/EndSpan/Annotate/RecordMetric. The shim serializes to a compact binary protobuf and sends over a fast unix domain socket to metrics-stitch.
- Build metrics-stitch (Go) as a single-process exporter that handles batching, retry/backoff, and adaptive batching based on queue pressure.
- Add feature flagging and canary rollout with traffic split (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
- Pin OTEL SDKs in other services and remove redundant vendor wrappers.
- Provide migration compatibility layer for legacy span consumers for 30 days.

Success metrics: binary size reduction >= 12% for hot-path worker, CPU usage drop >= 10% at p95 throughput in staging, no regression in end-to-end trace completeness (>99% of expected spans), and stable exporter queue length < 2s of buffered payload.

Rollout plan: dev -> staging (end-to-end test harness + load test) -> canary in prod (10% of requests for 24h) -> 50% -> 100%. Automated rollback on error budget breach or exporter error rate >0.5% for 10m.

Related artifacts: design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/62431/trace-shim-design, perf benches: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1PerfBenchExample, initial RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/182
comments: 2025-07-24 - Maya Chen: Spike complete. Implemented prototype trace-shim and local metrics-stitch. Local microbench: shim serialization adds ~120ns/span, vastly smaller than grpc+otlp stack. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821

2025-07-30 - Diego Alvarez: Architecture review with Observability and Runtime teams. Action items: add sampling compatibility tests, define emergency telemetry-only fallback path, and add more robust socket reconnection logic to shim.

2025-08-04 - SRE (Lina Patel): Load runner shows CPU p95 down 13% on worker-x when using shim + stitch under 10k rps. We still see occasional exporter backlog spikes when backend experiences transient 5xxs; metrics-stitch changes look good but needs backpressure signals upstream.

2025-08-07 - Maya Chen: Addressed backlog by adding adaptive batch window and max-batch-bytes. Updated PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4933. Unit and integration tests added. Marking for staging rollout on 2025-08-10.

2025-08-12 - QA (Evan Brooks): Staging e2e: trace completeness 99.4% for sample workload; additional failure mode: if metrics-stitch is OOM, legacy exporter fallback did not reattach. Added a watchdog to restart stitch and enable in-place fallback.

2025-08-14 - Maya Chen: Canary started at 5% (internal traffic). Observability dashboards added: shim/span-rate, stitch/queue-ms, stitch/export-errors, worker/binary-size. No regressions so far. Preparing rollout playbook and rollback steps.
